record.description: In 1908, an extraordinary event shook the remote forests of Siberia as a massive explosion flattened an area of 2,000 square kilometers. Known as the Tunguska event, this phenomenon occurred without leaving a crater. Scientists attribute it to a meteoroid or comet exploding in the atmosphere, unleashing energy 1,000 times greater than that of the Hiroshima bomb. However, the absence of solid fragments raises questions. While some propose theories—ranging from a comet to a mini black hole or even alien technology—these remain unproven. The Tunguska event endures as one of history’s greatest mysteries, with the true cause shrouded in uncertainty. What truly transpired over Siberia? We still don’t know.
record.idea: 1. The Tunguska event: What caused the massive 1908 Siberian explosion?

record.script: In 1908, a massive explosion flattened 2,000 square kilometers of Siberian forest—without a crater. Scientists say a meteoroid or comet exploded in the atmosphere, releasing energy 1,000 times that of Hiroshima. But no solid fragments were found. Some speculate it was a comet; others, a mini black hole or alien technology—but these remain unproven theories. To this day, the Tunguska event remains one of history’s greatest unsolved mysteries—an enormous blast with no clear cause. What truly happened over Siberia? We still don’t know.
